;Disasters and accidents
*[[Boeing 737 MAX groundings]]
**The [[European Union]], [[Australia]], [[India]], [[Malaysia]], [[Singapore]], and [[Turkey]] ground all [[Boeing 737 MAX 8]] jets. This means 40% of the global fleet is now grounded, with [[Indonesia]], [[China]] and several airlines grounding their aircraft yesterday. Boeing states they will issue a software update for the model within weeks. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/11/airlines-and-agencies-reassure-alarmed-passengers-about-boeing-737-max-8 (''The Guardian'')] [https://twitter.com/BNONews/status/1105506460237209601 (BNO)] [https://twitter.com/AFP/status/1105532685059932161 (AFP)]
*The sinking of the ''[[Grande America]]'' causes a {{convert|2200|t|lb}} oil spill in the [[Bay of Biscay]], France. [https://www.freightwaves.com/news/maritime/grimaldi-confirms-grande-america-fire-started-in-cargo-container-ezkx7-g33nr-gn3cf (''FreightWaves'')] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/royal-navy-rescue-container-ship-fire-hms-argyll-a8818536.html (''The Independent'')]
;International relations
*[[United States–Venezuela relations]], [[Crisis in Venezuela]]
**The [[United States Secretary of State]] [[Mike Pompeo]] announces that the U.S. will be withdrawing all remaining diplomatic staff from [[Venezuela]]. The withdrawal follows televised remarks from [[Nicolás Maduro]] calling ''[[Colectivo (Venezuela)|colectivos]]'' (paramilitary groups) to active resistance, and alleging that [[President of the United States|U.S. President]] [[Donald Trump]] masterminded the [[2019 Venezuelan blackout|ongoing nationwide power blackout]] as part of a "demonic plot" to oust him, by crippling the country's [[Electricity sector in Venezuela|electricity sector]] with an "electromagnetic attack". [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/12/nicolas-maduro-blames-demonic-trump-plot-for-blackout-crippling-venezuela (''The Guardian'')] [https://www.infobae.com/america/venezuela/2019/03/12/en-medio-del-masivo-apagon-en-venezuela-nicolas-maduro-llamo-a-los-colectivos-chavistas-a-la-resistencia-activa/ (Infobae)]
*In an annual report, the [[Estonian Foreign Intelligence Service]] warns that Russia will "very likely" try to intervene in European parliamentary elections this May to undermine unity within the European Union "by sowing disorder and disbelief" within and between the 28 [[European Union]] member states. [https://news.sky.com/story/russia-very-likely-to-meddle-in-european-parliament-elections-warns-estonia-spy-chief-11663051 (Sky News)]

;Law and crime
*[[2019 college admissions bribery scandal]]
**A college admission scheme across the [[United States]] results in the indictment of over 50 people including athletic coaches, CEOs, and two Hollywood actresses, accused of using bribery and fraud in order to cheat their children into universities such as [[Yale]] and [[Stanford]]. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/03/12/us/indictment-college-admissions-scheme/index.html (CNN)] [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-education-cheating/hollywoods-huffman-loughlin-snared-in-25-million-u-s-college-fraud-scheme-idUSKBN1QT1WJ (Reuters)]
*[[Catholic Church sexual abuse cases]]
**[[Cardinal (Catholic Church)|Cardinal]] [[George Pell]], the most senior official of the [[Catholic Church]] to be convicted of sexual abuse to date, is sentenced to six years in prison for the sexual assault of two children in the late 1990s. [https://www.cnn.com/2019/03/12/australia/cardinal-george-pell-sentencing-intl/index.html?no-st=1552451368 (CNN)]
*[[Capital punishment in California]]
**It is reported that [[California]] [[Governor of California|Governor]] [[Gavin Newsom]] will sign an executive order placing a [[moratorium (law)|moratorium]] on the death penalty for all 737 inmates on California's death row, ensuring that no executions will take place while he is governor. [https://www.dailynews.com/2019/03/12/gov-gavin-newsom-to-halt-death-penalty-despite-voter-efforts-to-hasten-executions/?utm_content=fb-ladailynews&utm_source=facebook.com&utm_medium=social&utm_campaign=socialflow (''Los Angeles Daily News'')]
*[[Crisis in Venezuela]], [[Censorship in Venezuela]]
**Prominent Venezuelan journalist {{ill|Luis Carlos Díaz|es}} is released after being taken by [[Bolivarian Intelligence Service|SEBIN]], the national intelligence service, on Monday; he has been ordered not to speak of his time in detention or publish anything. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2019/mar/12/venezuela-luis-carlos-diaz-journalist-taken-sebin (''The Guardian'')]
;Politics and elections
*[[2019 Micronesian parliamentary election]]
**[[President of the Federated States of Micronesia|President]] [[Peter M. Christian]] is defeated for re-election to his at-large seat in [[Congress of the Federated States of Micronesia|Congress]] by David Panuelo. [https://www.pacificislandtimes.com/single-post/2019/03/12/FSM-elections-certified-Peter-Christian-loses-seat-to-Panuelo (Pacific Islands Times)]
*[[Brexit negotiations]]
**The [[Parliament of the United Kingdom|UK's parliament]] rejects Prime Minister Theresa May's [[Brexit]] deal by 149 votes. A vote for leaving the European Union without a deal is scheduled for the thirteenth of March. If Parliament rejects the decision to leave with no deal, the UK could request its withdrawal from the EU be postponed with the unanimous consent of the other 27 member states. [https://www.nytimes.com/2019/03/12/world/europe/brexit-vote.html (''The New York Times'')]
